Decisions were made by General Kukanjac and the president of the Presidency of BiH, Alija Izetbegovic. Some units were deployed to Grahovo, Drvar, and --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: General --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: -- General Perisic's unit from Zadar was deployed to the centre of military schools, Josip Broz Tito in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. So when JNA mortars and artillery were deployed to areas ringing Sarajevo, in late 1991 and the beginning of 1992 that happened under your control; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: What I said is that the units were deployed only to the former JNA barracks. As regards Sarajevo, it regards the barracks at Lukavica and the school centre Josip Broz Tito in Sarajevo. As for other units, they were also deployed to different JNA barracks in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina, with the exception of Drvar, Bosanski Petrovac, where there were no JNA barracks. There the units were temporarily accommodated in the production facilities of a number of factories and sawmills.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: General, in no later than April 1992 the JNA 4th Corps artillery regiment and the 4th Corps anti-artillery regiment had units whose weapons were deployed -- has units who were deployed to areas in the elevations around the city of Sarajevo. That happened under your command; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: I had no influence whatsoever on the deployment of units or artillery. That decision was made solely by the commanding staff; in other words, General Kukanjac approved and the corps commander, General Djurdjevac, decided on where to deploy the units of his own corps that he was in command of. No other personnel under the existing regulations could have any bearing on where the units would be deployed, especially when it comes to artillery.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: You also told the Judges in the Perisic case that you believed that the Territorial Defence units under the command of the Serb authorities were armed by local Serb authorities and not by the JNA, and that's in the Perisic case transcript pages 12549 to -51. So I want to just ask you about that. Is it your evidence that the JNA was not involved in the arming of Serb volunteers?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: What I know and what I had documents about is that there were orders coming from the SSNO and the JNA General Staff to carry out mobilisation and additional mobilisation of the war time units of the JNA in the area of responsibility of the 2nd Military District. The basic goal of the exercise was to protect JNA property, its weapons and military equipment, and to have the resources exclusively under control of the commanding staff of the JNA. As of 1 March and until the 3rd of May, 1992, I was detained because I had been taken prisoner in the command building of the 2nd Military District together with other JNA members. Our telephone lines were cut off --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: General --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: -- as well as electricity --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: -- you spoke about parts of this in your written evidence. My question to you was whether it was your evidence that the JNA was not involved in the arming of Serb volunteers. I take it from your answer that it was?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Let me continue. Given the fact that I was detained for two months, I had no insight or influence over things happening in the field. I was physically unable to leave the building or communicate by phone. I do know that the JNA was responsible for carrying out mobilisations and to man the units; however, I do not know of, although I cannot exclude the possibility, that some Serb units as part of the Territorial Defence of Republika Srpska received weapons and, as such, were made part and placed under the command of the JNA. That is well possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, I'm a bit surprised to hear you say that and I'll show you something to -- and you'll see why.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we have a look, please, at P1477.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: It's a copy of the notebook of General Mladic covering the period from February to May 1992. And I'd like to look at e-court page 296 in English and page 303 in the B/C/S transcribed page. And in the original handwritten version it's page 305. I think we need to go over to the next page in B/C/S, please. There we go. Now, General, you've just told me you had no knowledge of the arming of Serbs by the JNA, but on 11 May 1992, after his meeting in Nevesinje that morning, General Mladic met with you, where you told him that you had been the assistant commander for logistics at the command of the 2nd Military District. And you said to him: "I have been the brains of the weapons distribution for 10 months and so far 69.000 Serbs have been armed. "I know the area, could I please stay on duty." General, by your own words as noted by your commander, not only did you know about the arming of Serbs by the JNA, but you ensured and you co-ordinated it in municipalities across Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: I never met General Kukanjac or Mladic or anybody else in Nevesinje. I claim with full responsibility that I had never been at Nevesinje at the time. It wasn't possible either because I was being treated after my injury which I sustained on Dobrovoljacka Street.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: You may have misunderstood me. My reference to Nevesinje was to a meeting that General Mladic had. This is a meeting with you as noted up in his notebook on 11 May 1992?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: I repeat that I've never been in Nevesinje with General Mladic. That is absolutely false. I never confirmed that nor could Mladic have noted that in his notebook. There is a Colonel Kovacevic in Nevesinje who was a commander of a unit there --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: General, I never said you were in Nevesinje. I said General Mladic was. All right? Have a look at what's on the page in front of you in your language --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we show him the handwriting version? Would it be more convenient for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: It may be. It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Or can we see the -- where does the date appear?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: A few pages previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So why don't we show the cover page and show him this is the diary which General Mladic kept at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And this is the handwritten version of that specific page that we see in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, yes. So let's find out this. Colonel Kovacevic was the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And this is the cover page of General Mladic's notebook that you see, General. And you were a colonel at this time. You didn't get to be general until January 1993?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: That is correct. But there was also Colonel Kovacevic in Nevesinje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The commander of the Nevesinje Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But the first paragraph of this diary says -- is referring to a colonel who is assistant commander for logistics at the 2nd Military District. So it must have been you, Mr. Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I was. I don't deny and I accept, or rather, it is correct that I met General Mladic at Lukavica. I don't know the exact date, but it was around the 15th of May. I don't know the exact date. What he may have written isn't anything I could influence. It is true that I followed the orders of General Kukanjac, the commander of the 2nd Military District, and the orders of the General Staff in Belgrade to arm the units mobilised in accordance with the establishment. Those were volunteer units, and the volunteers were mostly Serbs. But there were also members of other ethnicities, including Croats and Muslims. Major Anton Sinkovic was a Croat, and this can pertain to the establishing of JNA units in implementation of the order of mobilisation. But nobody ever directly issued weapons to groups of civilians or the Serbs in general. But since 99 per cent of the volunteers were Serbs, that was an imposed fact to keep the armaments and means of communication of the JNA because the goal was not to allow that weapons and military equipment be stolen and used without control in show-downs between members of the three ethnic communities, as had been the case in some barracks where people had been imprisoned, weapons, and military equipment stolen, and military units controlled by the Sarajevo government armed, mostly Muslim units but also Croatian HVO units.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So when you told us a few moments ago that you had no insight or influence into what was going on in terms of arming of the Serbs, that was actually incorrect. Just like you told General Mladic, you were the brains of the weapons distribution for ten months and so far 69.000 Serbs had been armed; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: That can be interpreted in various ways. I can tell you that this is completely unsuitable. Mladic could write down his opinion of me, but my role cannot have been any different than envisaged by the system of command and control in the JNA units --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: -- and I strictly adhered to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: General --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: -- Mladic's handwriting --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Let's -- on that note, let's look at another document and it's P5583. It's a speech delivered by Dr. Karadzic to the Herzegovina Corps command on 13 May 1995. Now, I would like us to go over to page 6 of the -- I think in both languages. In the second paragraph on page 6. And I just need to have a moment to see if I've got the right page in B/C/S. If not, I will read slowly in English. And my apologies to you, General. I haven't written down the right page in your language for your benefit. But Dr. Karadzic in his speech in May 1995 talked about the situation and looked back. He said: "It is a fact of the matter that we inherited a lot of things in the JNA storehouses and we managed to disperse a lot of things thanks to General Kovacevic who was a colonel at the time, and with the agreement between Krajisnik and myself and General Mladic, we managed to disperse a lot of things from the territories under the control of Croats and Muslims. That is how we inherited these things." So, General, by Dr. Karadzic's words, you weren't working according to the establishment, but you were working in the interests of Dr. Karadzic, Mr. Krajisnik, and General Mladic and according to their instructions?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. Could you please show me where I said that he was not working in accordance to establishment structures? Did he violate any rule of the federal ministry?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honours, what was my question. I read Dr. Karadzic's quotation onto the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But you were not working according to the establishment. It's not a quotation from this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And I apologise for any misunderstanding I might have caused of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: General, you said you were working according to the establishment. Dr. Karadzic in his speech says that you were working according to an agreement between he, Mr. Krajisnik, and General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: What is written here was allegedly said by Mr. Karadzic, but I have never heard or seen that so far nor has anybody showed me. I say with full responsibility that I received an order from the General Staff of the JNA, that is, General Kukanjac did. He was the commander. He acquainted me with that order and the order says that weapons and military equipment were to be removed from all military warehouses and facilities considered to be at risk because they could be attacked. Thus, uncontrolled paramilitaries could avail themselves of military equipment and weapons. That document was shown to me by the Defence these days and it is referenced in my statement. I can continue to say how that came about.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: No. General, I think what I'd like to do is continue to ask you questions. We'll go on to another area and it's something, as before, you didn't deal with in your statement but you did deal with it in your testimony during the Perisic case. And it's about your position in the Main Staff. Can you confirm that from September 1992 until January 1993 you were a member of the VRS Main Staff? That should be an easy yes or no question.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: I kindly ask you to return to the previous question because we haven't finished with it. You could allow me to enable the Trial Chamber to see that order from the General Staff in Belgrade which says that these assets should be removed, and I was in charge of that process --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: General --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: -- to remove military equipment to safe areas --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. Because my time with you has been very limited, I would not like to run afoul of any time-limits I have, and I'd like you to focus on my questions so that we can keep within the time-limits. And if there's anything that hasn't been covered, Dr. Karadzic should be able to raise this in his re-direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, that's correct. But in some instances the witness should be allowed to complete his answer and this is one of them because he obviously has something he wants to say. It's related to the topic and it's, I think, wrong for him to be cut off in this instance. And she can have an extension of the time if he needs it, but it's not a licence to make a witness not be able to give a complete answer that's relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I tend to agree. Mr. Kovacevic, did you finish your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If at all possible, I would kindly ask for the document at hand to be presented to the Trial Chamber so you see that it really exists. I asked the Defence to insist on my claim that I worked pursuant to that order, whereas there is no evidence that I worked pursuant to the demands of the Dr. Karadzic or Mr. Krajisnik. So the Trial Chamber should be shown the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If necessary, the Defence will take up that issue in its re-examination. In the meantime, please proceed, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So you were a member of the VRS Main Staff from September 1992 until January 1993; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And you worked as an administrator for General Djukic who was the Main Staff assistant commander for logistics; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: But you weren't one of the core members of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't a man who decided about anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And following your appointment as defence minister and for the remainder of the war, you didn't take part in any Main Staff discussions or meetings or briefings whatsoever; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: I was present at a number of meetings of the Main Staff. I was invited there as minister of defence, mostly to discussions about the combat-readiness of the units of the VRS, especially when the supply situation of the VRS was discussed. I was also present at Supreme Command meetings. As a member of the Supreme Command in my capacity as minister of defence. There are two --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Can I just ask you first off --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: -- mostly logistic matters were discussed.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Let me just ask you about that, and we'll come back to your presence at Main Staff meetings because that's something that wasn't in your statement. When you took part in Supreme Command meetings, that was between January 1993 and August 1994 and no later; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And when you testified in the Perisic case, you told the Judges there that Supreme Command meetings didn't happen according to set dates. They took place just whenever the circumstances dictated; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Mostly when some circumstance required an urgent meeting, then a meeting of the Supreme Command was called.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And we'll get into the Supreme Command a little bit more tomorrow, but I also just before we close today, I want to ask you one quick question, and it's on the subject of your appointment to the position of defence minister. You talked about it in your statement at paragraph 18 and you said that Vladimir Lukic summoned you to Pale and he told you there that he was going to put you forward as minister of defence. But, in fact, Dr. Karadzic was there as well during that meeting, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vladimir Lukic invited me to Pale and I went there to meet him. He was the first to inform me that he would nominate me for the position of minister of defence. We went to see Mr. Karadzic together, and I put forward my position. First of all, I asked whether the Main Staff of the VRS was backing up that nomination, and President Karadzic was present on that occasion. He said that the Main Staff was not opposed to my appointment.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And the evidence that Dr. Karadzic was there or you took part in a meeting with Dr. Karadzic at that moment, that's not in your statement either, is it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: I no longer remember what I said in these statements. Much time has passed, but surely Lukic must have asked that we meet President Karadzic so that I might accept or refuse that.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: All right. Tomorrow morning I'll bring you a copy of the statement you signed for Dr. Karadzic's Defence in case you find it easier to have it with you while we continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll adjourn for today, Mr. Kovacevic, and continue tomorrow morning at 9.00. I'd like to advise you not to discuss with anybody else about your testimony. Do you understand that, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 11th day of June, 2013, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.46 p.m.,
